hookLine: Charlie and Maria Cardoso owned their house outright, and a bank's contractors still emptied it, because somewhere a clerk was signing sworn statements at a rate no human being could read.

HOOK.secondary: Charlie Cardoso cuts the padlocks off his own front door

OP.secondary: A couple buy somewhere to retire to, on the Gulf side of Florida

ACT_1.secondary: New Bedford, Massachusetts — a fishing city on the south coast
Three bedrooms and a pool, a few blocks south of Spring Hill Drive

ACT_1.label: Paid in cash — Charlie's life savings, the complaint says

ACT_1.secondary: No lender, no lien, no note, no monthly payment — and a deed stamped by the Hernando County recorder

ACT_1.label: Loans the Cardosos ever had with Bank of America or Countrywide

ACT_1.secondary: The tenant telephones in a panic: three Bank of America men are there to foreclose
Contacted Bank of America to advise it that it was foreclosing on the wrong home

ACT_1.quote: Their own real estate agent told them, and nevertheless Bank of America steamrolled right ahead.
ACT_1.attribution: the Cardosos' attorney, to the St. Petersburg Times, 13 February 2010

ACT_1.primary: THE HOUSE THEY MEANT TO TAKE
ACT_1.secondary: Across the street, about ten doors down

events.text: The bank's landscaping crew breaks the fence to get its mowers in
The frightened tenant moves out for good
Bank of America's people come back and padlock the house again

ACT_2.secondary: A representative checks the file and says the bank had made a mistake

ACT_2.quote: Countrywide/BOA never called Mr. Cardoso back that day or any day thereafter.
ACT_2.attribution: Cardoso v. Bank of America, second amended complaint, D. Mass. 1:10-cv-10075

ACT_2.label: Massachusetts to Florida — his son put him in a car and drove him

ACT_2.secondary: Maria's son was coming home from his third tour in Iraq
The police finally agree to let him into his own house

ACT_2.quote: he cut all the locks off the doors and had to break into the back screen door to get in.
ACT_2.attribution: Cardoso v. Bank of America, second amended complaint, paragraph 21

ACT_2.secondary: Air compressor, nail gun, table saw, lawnmower, two refrigerators, the gas grill, the family photographs

ACT_2.primary: FROZEN PIPES, A DEAD POOL PUMP
ACT_2.secondary: Water and power shut off, tire tracks across the lawn — only the attic was untouched
The Cardosos file suit in federal court in Massachusetts

ACT_2.quote: We have reached out to the Cardosos' representatives and hope to have the opportunity to work with them to properly assess and address their allegations.

ACT_2.label: American homes that completed foreclosure — the peak year
Foreclosures completed in the worst single month

ACT_3.secondary: One named person swears, on penalty of perjury, that they have read the file

ACT_3.primary: IN A GREAT MANY CASES IT IS THE ONLY EVIDENCE
ACT_3.secondary: Most homeowners in foreclosure have no lawyer; many never appear at all
Christopher Immel of Ice Legal puts the question to a man named Jeffrey Stephan
Team leader of the document execution unit, a team of fourteen — GMAC Mortgage, Fort Washington, Pennsylvania

ACT_3.quote: in a month, my team brings to me approximately, I'd say a round number of 10,000. That's just an estimate, of course.

items.label: DOCUMENTS BROUGHT TO HIM IN A MONTH
MINUTES IN AN EIGHT-HOUR WORKING MONTH

ACT_3.quote: So these documents wouldn't be actually executed on your own personal knowledge? — Right.
ACT_3.attribution: Christopher Immel and Jeffrey Stephan, sworn deposition, 10 December 2009

ACT_3.secondary: The notaries were not physically present, and he agreed that this was common
Maine lawyer Thomas Cox deposes him a second time, in a second case

ACT_3.label: New requests a day, on his own sworn testimony

ACT_3.attribution: Jeffrey Stephan, asked what he reads before signing, 7 June 2010

ACT_3.quote: So you do not appear before the notary; is that correct? — I do not.
ACT_3.attribution: Thomas Cox and Jeffrey Stephan, sworn deposition, 7 June 2010

ACT_3.label: Costs the Maine court ordered the plaintiff to pay, finding the affidavit submitted in bad faith

ACT_3.quote: The affidavit in this case is a disturbing example of a reprehensible practice. That such fraudulent evidentiary filings are being submitted to courts is both violative of the rules of court and ethically indefensible.
ACT_3.attribution: Federal National Mortgage Ass'n v. Bradbury, Maine Supreme Judicial Court, 2011

ACT_3.secondary: A Florida court had already sanctioned the very same company for the very same practice

ACT_4.secondary: A low-rise office suite, owned by Lender Processing Services of Jacksonville, Florida

ACT_4.label: Fraudulently signed and notarised mortgage documents, filed with property recorders

ACT_4.quote: a six-year scheme to prepare and file more than 1 million fraudulently signed and notarized mortgage-related documents with property recorders' offices throughout the United States.
ACT_4.attribution: United States Department of Justice, 25 June 2013

ACT_4.label: DocX gross revenue over those six years

ACT_4.secondary: An auto-parts shipping clerk who took a job at DocX in 2003 — she was never charged with anything

ACT_4.quote: She told us she has never been a bank vice president.
So you're Linda Green? — Yeah, can't you tell?
ACT_4.attribution: Scott Pelley and DocX signer Chris Pendley, CBS, April 2011

ACT_4.label: Signatures an hour — the floor quota at DocX

ACT_4.quote: So if Chris Pendley was signing for Linda Green, you'd notarize that document. — Yes.
ACT_4.attribution: Scott Pelley and DocX signer and notary Shawanna Crite, CBS, April 2011

ACT_4.quote: Thousands and thousands and thousands of assignments . . . signed weekly.
ACT_4.attribution: Florida Attorney General, Economic Crimes Division presentation, December 2010

ACT_4.label: Banks the name was signed as vice president of at the same time — investigator Lynn Szymoniak, in her own foreclosure file

ACT_4.secondary: A Bank of America official said she signed 7,000 to 8,000 foreclosure documents a month without reading them

events.text: GMAC Mortgage tells brokers and agents to halt evictions in 23 states
JPMorgan Chase suspends more than 50,000 foreclosures
Bank of America freezes foreclosures in the same 23 states
Bank of America extends the freeze to all fifty

ACT_4.label: 23 STATES WHERE A JUDGE MUST BE HANDED THE PAPER

events.text: Attorneys general from all fifty states announce a joint investigation
Bank of America says it will process affidavits in 102,000 proceedings
Wells Fargo will file supplemental affidavits in 55,000 foreclosure actions

ACT_5.title: THE PRICE OF A MILLION HOMES

ACT_5.secondary: Justice, HUD, 49 state attorneys general and the District of Columbia — every state except Oklahoma — against the five biggest servicers

ACT_5.label: The National Mortgage Settlement, as announced

ACT_5.quote: This agreement – the largest joint federal-state settlement ever obtained – is the result of unprecedented coordination among enforcement agencies throughout the government.

items.label: CASH TO PEOPLE WHOSE HOMES WERE TAKEN ($BN)

ACT_5.label: Share of the twenty-five billion that was cash to a person whose house had already been taken
What each of those households received — the settlement had been sized for about three quarters of a million claims

ACT_5.quote: a pattern of misconduct and negligence related to deficient practices in residential mortgage loan servicing and foreclosure processing
ACT_5.attribution: consent orders against fourteen banking organisations, 13 April 2011

ACT_5.secondary: The Independent Foreclosure Review is terminated — final reviews were done on about 14 per cent of the files, and no consultant finished a sample

items.label: WHAT THE REVIEWS WOULD RETURN TO THE HARMED ($BN)

ACT_5.quote: regardless of whether the borrower had suffered financial injury caused by servicer error
ACT_5.attribution: Federal Reserve, Independent Foreclosure Review Final Report, 2019

ACT_5.label: Out of 3,949,896 borrowers in the Federal Reserve's own payment table, published 9 April 2013
Every one a servicemember whose home was foreclosed in breach of a law written to protect people on active duty

ACT_5.secondary: Chief executive of DocX — pleaded guilty 20 November 2012, sentenced 25 June 2013 to five years in prison and a $15,000 fine

ACT_5.label: Paid by Lender Processing Services under a non-prosecution agreement, four months before she was sentenced
The cheque a branch manager wrote within the hour, after the Nyerges' lawyer arrived with deputies and a moving truck

ENDING.label: Roughly, completed foreclosures in the United States, on CoreLogic's count

ENDING.quote: Between 2006 and 2008, the number of foreclosure filings increased threefold from 700,000 to 2.3 million.

ENDING.secondary: Loans most homeowners last paid in 2015 or earlier, sold to debt collectors for pennies on the dollar
The Bureau found one or more companies had failed to send those homeowners the statements the law requires

ENDING.quote: issuing stop-work orders; closing supervisory examinations; and terminating employees, contracts, and enforcement cases
ENDING.attribution: GAO-26-108448, on the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau since February 2025

ENDING.primary: A FEDERAL COURT HAS SO FAR BLOCKED THE PLAN
ENDING.secondary: The funding cap was cut in half by statute in July 2025; the litigation is live as this film goes out
